title: 16-bit toggle timer clock divider
description: Select a 16-bit timer compare value by nearest output-period rounding for a supplied hardware prescaler, and calculate actual frequency error.
formula: count = floor(f_clock/(2 P f_target)+0.5); compare = count-1; f_actual = f_clock/(2 P count)
assumptions: Timer counts inclusively from zero through compare and toggles its output once per compare event; two toggles make one output cycle.
16-bit compare register and common AVR-style prescalers 1, 8, 64, 256 or 1024; verify the selected device supports the chosen prescaler and toggle mode.
Nearest period count with half-integer ties rounded upward; not guaranteed to minimize absolute frequency error.
No automatic prescaler selection, fractional divider, oscillator tolerance or transient register-update behavior.

references.title: Microchip AVR timer: Clear Timer on Compare Match mode, toggle-output frequency
Microchip ATmega640/1280/1281/2560/2561 datasheet, timer CTC mode

constraints.message: Prescaler must be one of 1, 8, 64, 256 or 1024.
Target exceeds the maximum toggle-output frequency.
Rounded count exceeds the 16-bit compare-register range.

title: Finite-edge lumped capacitive crosstalk
description: Estimate the peak victim-node excursion caused by a linear aggressor edge through mutual capacitance, including victim resistance and shunt capacitance.
formula: tau = R_v(C_m+C_v); x = t_edge/tau; V_divider = C_m DeltaV/(C_m+C_v); V_peak = V_divider [-expm1(-x)/x]
assumptions: Ideal stiff aggressor source with a linear full-swing ramp; victim initially at its resistor-defined DC potential.
Victim has constant resistance to AC ground and shunt capacitance; mutual capacitance also contributes to victim time constant.
Coupled segment propagation delay must not exceed one tenth of the ramp duration, a conservative lumped-model selection criterion.
Magnetic coupling, distributed near/far-end crosstalk, multiple aggressors, clamps and nonlinear victim input behavior are excluded.
Peak is an excursion magnitude at the end of the ramp; if it reaches clamp thresholds the linear estimate is no longer the realized waveform.

Native expm1 preserves the capacitive-divider fast-edge limit for representable positive edge/time-constant ratios, including x about 1e-16; no artificial minimum ratio is imposed. The attenuation quotient is computed before multiplying by the divider voltage. Nonfinite intermediates or a ratio that underflows to zero must be rejected explicitly by the shared engine.

references.title: TI/National SNOA382: Understanding and Eliminating EMI in Microcontroller Applications, sections 3.6 and 4.5-4.6
MIT 6.071: Capacitors and inductors, capacitor current law and KCL

constraints.message: Propagation delay must be at most one tenth of edge time for this lumped estimate.

title: UART baud mismatch and stop-sample margin
description: Estimate the worst first-stop-bit sampling margin from independent transmitter and receiver baud rates, frame length and start-edge quantization.
formula: n = 1 + data_bits + parity_bits + 0.5; early = n/B_rx - (n-0.5)/B_tx - guard; late = (n+0.5)/B_tx - n/B_rx - 1/(S B_rx) - guard
assumptions: One start bit and one stop bit, independent constant baud clocks, ideal bit boundaries, and sample times centered relative to the detected start edge.
Start-edge detection is delayed by between zero and one oversample tick; no early-detection offset or mid-frame resynchronization.
A single center sample is modeled; majority voting, receiver-specific filters, fractional dividers and exact manufacturer tolerance tables are not modeled.
The optional guard subtracts additional settling/jitter allowance at each stop-bit boundary.
Positive minimum margin is only a necessary timing-budget result for this simplified receiver model, not proof of communication reliability. Negative margin identifies a possible framing failure.

references.title: Microchip USART: Asynchronous Receiver, oversampling and stop-bit sampling
Microchip AVR USART: Asynchronous Data Reception, center-sample majority voting

outputs.label: Receiver baud error relative to transmitter

constraints.message: Data bit count must be an integer.
Parity bit count must be zero or one.

title: Parallel-plate displacement current
description: Estimate edge-driven common-mode displacement current through a rectangular dielectric overlap to a chassis or reference plane.
formula: C = epsilon_0 epsilon_r width length/gap; slew = DeltaV/t_edge; I_displacement = C slew; J_displacement = I/(width length)
assumptions: Rectangular parallel conducting surfaces separated by a homogeneous linear, nonmagnetic dielectric; zero conductive leakage.
Gap must be at most one tenth of both plate dimensions to neglect fringing; this is a model-selection approximation, not a guaranteed error bound.
Longest plate dimension must be at most one tenth of the distance light travels in the dielectric during the full ramp, a conservative quasistatic criterion.
Use relative permittivity appropriate to the edge spectrum. Signed voltage change sets current direction; return-network impedance and radiation are not solved.
Does not certify EMC emissions, safety leakage, isolation withstand or dielectric breakdown.

references.title: MIT 6.013 Electromagnetics and Applications: chapter 3, equations 3.1.10-3.1.12 and displacement-current term in 3.2.1

inputs.label: Signed voltage change across the overlap

constraints.message: Gap must be at most one tenth of each plate dimension for the no-fringing approximation.
Plate dimensions must be electrically short for the quasistatic estimate.

title: I2C pullup resistance bounds
description: Find the pullup resistor interval allowed by open-drain sink capability and a 30%-to-70% bus rise-time limit.
formula: R_min = (V_supply - V_OL)/I_sink; R_max = t_r/[ln(7/3) C_bus]; width = R_max - R_min
assumptions: Single lumped bus capacitance and passive resistor pullup; no rise-time accelerator or active pullup.
Rise time is measured between 30% and 70% of the supply.
Use the weakest device's guaranteed sink capability and actual mode-specific rise-time limit; leakage, resistor tolerance and capacitance tolerance require additional margin.
Negative interval width means no feasible passive pullup, not a recommended resistor; this estimate does not establish I2C compliance.

references.title: TI SLVA689: I2C Bus Pullup Resistor Calculation, equations 1-6

inputs.label: Guaranteed sink current at output-low limit

outputs.label: Feasible resistance interval width (negative means infeasible)

constraints.message: Output-low limit must be below the pullup supply.

title: RC Schmitt-input digital delay bounds
description: Bound the output transition time of a rising RC input using guaranteed Schmitt threshold and intrinsic gate-delay limits.
assumptions: Capacitor starts at zero and charges through a constant resistance toward a stiff supply after an ideal step.
Input has Schmitt hysteresis and permits slow input edges; ordinary CMOS inputs may oscillate or draw excess current.
Threshold bounds and gate-delay bounds must come from the selected device at the applicable supply, load and temperature.
R and C are fixed supplied values; repeat with tolerance corners for component variation. Input leakage, driver resistance variation and supply ramps are excluded.
This is a digital threshold-to-output timing window, not a general analog charging calculator.

references.title: TI SN74AHC14 datasheet: section 8.2, RC logic delay application and guaranteed threshold bounds

constraints.message: Minimum threshold cannot exceed maximum threshold.
Thresholds must be below the final input voltage.
Minimum gate delay cannot exceed maximum gate delay.
